terms.gloss: thus, so, in this way; like this
evidence: Cic. Fam. 2.15.2: sed quid agās? sīc vīvitur
Plaut. Bacch. 675: sīc hoc digitulīs duōbus sūmēbās prīmōribus? (“were you picking it up like this, with two fingertips?”)
terms.comment: Points back to what was just said, or, with a gesture, to what the speaker shows: “like this” (Lewis & Short: colloquial, mostly in comedy). As an answer, sīc est is “that’s right”.

terms.gloss: so, thus, in such a way
evidence: Cic. Att. 7.8.4: factum est ita (Lewis & Short)
Ter. And. 192: Ita ajunt (“so they say”)
terms.comment: The same “so”, but most often with a clause to follow: ita … ut, so … that. Alone as an answer it is “yes”.

phrases.latin: sīc igitur vīvitur: cotīdiē aliquid legitur aut scrībitur
phrases.english: so this is how we live: every day something is read or written
but what can you do? That’s life

phrases.latin: quod hodiē nōn est, crās erit: sīc vīta trūditur
phrases.english: what isn’t here today will be here tomorrow: that’s how life pushes on

sources: Lewis & Short: sic · Lewis & Short: ita
